title: Virtual colonoscopy (CT colonography)
what: CT images of your large bowel. The bowel is gently inflated with air. No tube with a camera is used.
why: To look for polyps if a regular colonoscopy is not possible or could not be completed, or if your doctor decides.
duration: usually 15 to 20 minutes in the room, plus bowel prep the day before; the report in 1 to 2 days
tell_doctor: Diabetes. Your prep and medicines will need to be adjusted
Allergy to iodine or contrast dye, or kidney disease
If you are or might be pregnant

prepare.title: 1 to 2 days before
prepare.text: A low-fiber diet: no vegetables, fruit, seeds, nuts, or beans. Ask the clinic for your plan.

prepare.title: Bowel prep
prepare.text: The day before, you drink a bowel prep solution as your doctor says. A special contrast to mark stool is often added.

prepare.title: On the day
prepare.text: Usually no food. Drink clear liquids as the clinic tells you.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor. They will decide.

steps: A thin, soft tube is placed in your bottom
Air or carbon dioxide is passed through it to open up the bowel
Sometimes a medicine is given into a vein to relax the bowel
Images are taken while you lie on your back and on your stomach. You need to hold your breath
feel: Bloating and cramps while the gas is added
It does not hurt, and the feelings pass quickly after the test
after: You will pass gas over the next hour. This is normal
If polyps are found, your doctor usually sends you for a regular colonoscopy to remove them
red_flags: Severe belly pain, a hard belly, a fever, or bleeding from the bottom: call emergency services

faq.q: Can I skip the bowel prep?
faq.a: No. Leftover stool can hide a polyp or look like one.

faq.q: Does it replace a regular colonoscopy?
faq.a: Not always. With CT, a polyp cannot be removed or sampled. Your doctor chooses.

reminders.text: Virtual colonoscopy tomorrow. Today, follow your diet and bowel prep plan.
